concept.name: Preliminary supply
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (PSY) in which large interests begin unloading shares in quantity after a pronounced advance, marked by expanding volume and widening price spread that signal a change of trend may be approaching. It mirrors preliminary support at market tops.
concept.intuition: The first time in a long climb that heavy selling shows up and noticeably slows the rise.
concept.mechanics: During an uptrend, the analyst watches for bars where volume and spread expand but upward progress stalls; that selling interest is labeled preliminary supply. PSY typically precedes the buying climax and begins Phase A of a distribution trading range.
concept.failure_modes: A single heavy-volume stall day can be absorbed and the advance can continue; PSY warns of possible topping but gives no information about how much further the rally may extend.
concept.misconceptions: Preliminary supply is not the top and does not warrant shorting by itself; confirmation requires the buying climax, automatic reaction, and secondary tests that follow.
concept.example: After doubling in a year, a stock posts record volume on a wide-range day that closes near unchanged; the analyst marks it as preliminary supply and watches for climactic buying.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
